Overview

LMI is seeking an experienced Deputy Program Manager / Operations Lead
to support the delivery of next-generation software capabilities for U.S. Army modernization initiatives. This position requires an Active Secret security clearance.

Reporting to the Technical Program Manager (TPM), this role serves as the operational backbone of the program, ensuring that staffing, financial management, contract administration, reporting, governance, and day-to-day business operations are executed efficiently so technical teams can remain focused on delivering mission-critical software.

The Deputy Program Manager will coordinate across corporate functions, Army stakeholders, subcontractors, and internal program leadership to ensure program execution remains aligned with contractual requirements, financial objectives , and organizational priorities. This position is ideal for someone who thrives in fast-paced, high-visibility software programs and enjoys building repeatable operational processes that enable successful software delivery.

Join a growing software organization delivering next-generation capabilities that directly support U.S. Army modernization efforts. As the Deputy Program Manager / Operations Lead, you'll play a critical role in ensuring the operational excellence that enables engineering teams to rapidly deliver secure, mission-ready software. Working alongside Technical Program Managers, Product Owners, Engineering Leads, Scrum Masters, software engineers, and Army stakeholders, you'll help build the operational foundation that allows innovative software solutions to move quickly from development to deployment.

LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed.

Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, healthcare, and energy sectors—helping agencies navigate complexity and outpace change. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia, LMI is committed to delivering impactful results that strengthen missions and drive lasting value.

Program Operations & Governance

Support the Technical Program Manager in executing day-to-day program operations across multiple software development workstreams.
Develop and maintain program management plans, integrated schedules, operational dashboards, and governance artifacts.
Coordinate program reviews, status meetings, leadership updates, and customer engagements.
Monitor program performance across cost, schedule, staffing, deliverables, and operational metrics.
Develop and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs), operational playbooks, templates, and governance documentation.
Coordinate contract deliverables and reporting requirements to ensure timely , accurate submission.

Business & Financial Operations

Track program budgets, labor utilization , burn rates, staffing forecasts, and financial performance.
Coordinate with corporate finance, contracts, recruiting, procurement, and security teams to support successful program execution.
Prepare monthly financial reports, operational summaries, and executive dashboards for program leadership.
Identify financial, contractual, and operational risks while recommending mitigation strategies.

Track resource utilization and forecast future staffing requirements.
Support personnel onboarding, training coordination, and workforce planning.
Monitor administrative compliance activities, including time reporting, training completion, and required documentation.
Foster strong collaboration between LMI employees, subcontractors, and customer organizations.

Communications & Executive Reporting

Prepare executive briefings, decision memoranda, monthly status reports, and customer-facing presentations.
Develop dashboards and reporting products that communicate program health, milestones, financial status, risks, and accomplishments.
Schedule and coordinate internal and external meetings, capturing action items and ensuring timely follow-up.
Support strategic communications across program leadership, corporate stakeholders, subcontractors, and Army customers.

Risk & Operational Excellence

Maintain program risk, issue, and action item logs while coordinating mitigation activities.
Support internal audits, program reviews, customer inspections, and compliance assessments.
Assist with contract modifications, change requests, staffing adjustments, and operational process improvements.
Continuously improve operational processes that enable predictable, scalable software delivery across the program.

Required Qualifications

Active Secret security clearance is required.
Bachelor's degree in Business Administration , Management, Information Systems, or a related discipline.
7+ years of experience supporting program, project, or business operations within complex government or defense programs.
Experience supporting software development, technology, or digital transformation programs.
Demonstrated experience managing program financials, staffing coordination, contract administration, reporting, and operational governance.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with experience preparing executive-level briefings and reports.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and other business productivity tools.
Proven ability to coordinate across multiple organizations while managing competing priorities.

Master's degree (MBA or related field).
PMP certification or equivalent.
Experience supporting Department of Defense software programs.
Familiarity with Agile software development environments.
Experience supporting cloud-native software, DevSecOps , RMF, or secure software delivery programs.
Experience supporting geographically distributed teams.

Two years direct experience with auxiliary, electrical and damage control systems for U.S. Naval Ships.
Two years of supervisory experience.

Knowledge of best practice maritime processes and support methodologies to meet Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO) requirements.
Ability to lead and manage large teams.
Ability to operate personal computers and have good knowledge and operational abilities with Microsoft Office tools.

Job Description

TPA Core Services Business Analyst

Contribute to the strategic direction of the business and support impactful mission outcomes as a TPA Core Services Business Analyst at GDIT. Here, you’ll enable the success of one of the most critical federal healthcare missions and support high-quality administrative services for the World Trade Center Health Program.

MEANINGFUL WORK AND PERSONAL IMPACT

As a TPA Core Services Business Analyst, the work you’ll do at GDIT will directly support the mission of the World Trade Center Health Program (WTCHP). You will play a crucial role in ensuring business requirements, workflows, and system interactions across Third Party Administrator (TPA) core services are clear, aligned, and ready for accurate and compliant healthcare delivery.

Lead requirements elicitation, documentation, and refinement activities that directly support eligibility, claims, provider management, member services, and payment workflows.
Collaborate with cross-functional technical teams, operational staff, system vendors, QA testers, and government stakeholders to ensure requirements and workflows align with system capabilities and mission needs.
Drive accurate outcomes by validating workflow logic, supporting testing efforts, ensuring requirements traceability, and resolving issues that impact TPA operations.
Utilize requirements management tools, workflow modeling skills, healthcare administrative expertise, and integration analysis techniques to support seamless operational execution.

What You’ll Need To Succeed

Bring your initiative and drive for innovation to GDIT. The TPA Core Services Business Analyst must have:

Education: Technical training, certification(s), or degree
Experience: 3+ years of related experience (healthcare operations, payer systems, or federal program support preferred)
Technical skills: Experience with requirements management, workflow/process mapping, EDI or API integrations, eligibility and claims systems, Jira, Confluence, Azure DevOps, or similar platforms
Security clearance level: MB(T2)
US citizenship required
Role requirements: Ability to collaborate with technical and operational teams; familiarity with HIPAA and secure handling of PHI/PII; experience validating system behavior; 0-10% travel as needed

GDIT IS YOUR PLACE

At GDIT, the mission is our purpose, and our people are at the center of everything we do.

Growth: AI-powered career tool that identifies career steps and learning opportunities
Support: An internal mobility team focused on helping you achieve your career goals
Rewards: Comprehensive benefits and wellness packages, 401K with company match, and competitive pay and paid time off
Flexibility: Full-flex work week to own your priorities at work and at home
Community: Award-winning culture of innovation and a military-friendly workplace

OWN YOUR OPPORTUNITY

Explore a career at GDIT and you’ll find endless opportunities to grow alongside colleagues who share your passion for the mission and for delivering reliable and meaningful results.

Total Rewards At GDIT

Our benefits package for all US-based employees includes a variety of medical plan options, some with Health Savings Accounts, dental plan options, a vision plan, and a 401(k) plan offering the ability to contribute both pre and post-tax dollars up to the IRS annual limits and receive a company match. To encourage work/life balance, GDIT offers employees full flex work weeks where possible and a variety of paid time off plans, including vacation, sick and personal time, holidays, paid parental, military, bereavement and jury duty leave. GDIT typically provides new employees with 15 days of paid leave per calendar year to be used for vacations, personal business, and illness and an additional 10 paid holidays per year. Paid leave and paid holidays are prorated based on the employee’s date of hire. The GDIT Paid Family Leave program provides a total of up to 160 hours of paid leave in a rolling 12 month period for eligible employees. To ensure our employees are able to protect their income, other offerings such as short and long-term disability benefits, life, accidental death and dismemberment, personal accident, critical illness and business travel and accident insurance are provided or available. We regularly review our Total Rewards package to ensure our offerings are competitive and reflect what our employees have told us they value most.

Our Identity Verification Process

As part of the hiring process, we will ask you to complete an identity verification process that leverages advanced biometrics and artificial intelligence to ensure authenticity and protect against identity fraud. You are expected to be on camera during virtual interviews. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud. By proceeding, you authorize the collection, processing, and use of your biometric data for identity verification and security purposes.
